title: k8s-node-lifecycle-debug-notes
content:
Context:
- Incident: Intermittent node NotReady / crashloop during spot instance reclaim window on Dedicated cluster (us-west-2a). Observed after recent kubelet + containerd upgrade via helm-operator job.
- Affected autoscaling group: asg-dedicated-gpu-usw2a (mixed instances).
- Symptoms: pods fail scheduling, kubelet shows repeated disconnects, node reboots or gets marked NotReady, kube-proxy flakes.

Commands I ran (raw, chronological):
1) Quick surface check
   kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels   <-- saw nodes cycling NotReady
   kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep <node-name>

2) Describe and logs
   kubectl describe node ip-10-0-1-23
   # relevant snippet from describe:
   # Conditions: Ready=False  (KubeletNotReady) since 2026-02-28T14:03:21Z
   #   Kubelet has encountered repeated failures connecting to the container runtime

   journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
   # saw: 
   # E0228 14:02:09.123456    1234 kubelet_node_status.go:89] Error updating node status: Get "http://127.0.0.1:10248/healthz": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:10248: connect: connection refused

   sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200 --no-pager
   # containerd errors: 
   # time="2026-02-28T14:01:58Z" level=error msg="containerd: failed to set up sandbox container" err="failed to create container for task: ... permission denied"

3) Node service state
   ssh ec2-user@ip-10-0-1-23
   sudo systemctl status docker || sudo systemctl status containerd
   # containerd was active but many failed create events.

4) Cordon/Drain (to get pods off and repro)
   kubectl cordon ip-10-0-1-23
   kubectl drain ip-10-0-1-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
   # drain hung on a pod stuck Terminating (local storage). Had to delete pod with --force --grace-period=0

5) Check CNI and kube-proxy
   kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | egrep "calico|weave|cilium|kube-proxy"
   kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-proxy-ip-10-0-1-23 -c kube-proxy
   # kube-proxy reported iptables restore errors: 
   # iptables-restore v1.8.7 (nf_tables): Couldn't load match `conntrack':No such file or directory

6) Helm/upgrade context (recent change)
   # we rolled containerd/kubelet via helm chart infra-agent 2026-02-27 23:45 UTC
   helm list -n infra|grep agent
   helm history infra-agent -n infra
   helm get values infra-agent -n infra

Error snippets captured (copy/paste):
- kubelet: "Error updating node status: Get \"http://127.0.0.1:10248/healthz\": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:10248: connect: connection refused"
- containerd: "failed to create container for task ... permission denied"
- iptables: "Couldn't load match `conntrack':No such file or directory"
- kernel: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" (seen earlier in dmesg)

Hypotheses so far:
- H1: Kernel modules (nf_conntrack/conntrack) missing or module parameters changed after AMI update => iptables/nft mismatch causing kube-proxy to fail and connection drops.
- H2: containerd binaries/config changed by recent helm upgrade; sandbox runtime permissions incorrect (seccomp/apparmor) causing container creation failures and kubelet to report runtime unavailable.
- H3: Spot instance reclaim/reboot timing + kubelet config (eviction thresholds) causes flapping and POSIX permissions race on overlayfs leading to stuck Terminating pods.
- H4: Mixed AMI family in ASG (some nodes still on old kernel) => kernel module mismatch + iptables vs nft conflicts.

Quick checks to validate hypotheses:
- Verify kernel modules: sudo lsmod | egrep conntrack; sudo modprobe nf_conntrack; dmesg | tail -n50 - Result: nf_conntrack module not loaded on one repro node; modprobe succeeds manually which transiently fixes iptables errors.
- Check AMI/kernel versions: uname -a; cat /etc/os-release - Found two flavors: amzn2-aws-k8s-1.25 (old) and amzn2-eks-optimized-1.26 (new).
- Check containerd config and binary checksum: sudo cat /etc/containerd/config.toml; sha256sum /usr/bin/containerd; compare to golden artifact in infra repo. - Found mismatched containerd binary on one node (older sha) => indicates image/AMI drift or post-launch package step.

Remediation attempts (notes):
- Temporary: modprobe nf_conntrack on nodes to restore kube-proxy iptables match and reduce packet drops. Monitored node status; some returned to Ready.
- Replaced node (terminate instance in ASG, allow scale up) to force fresh AMI that has consistent artifact set. Observed new node healthy.
- Rolled back infra-agent helm release to previous revision for a short window (helm rollback infra-agent 2 -n infra) to see if containerd change introduced regressions. After rollback, containerd errors reduced.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Reproduce in staging: create mixed-AMI ASG, run helm upgrade of infra-agent, observe module and containerd behaviour. Capture exact package diff.
- Add an infra check in ASG lifecycle hook to validate containerd binary checksum post-provisioning (systemd unit or cloud-init step). If mismatch, fail init and surface via node-label.
- Harden kube-proxy iptables fallback: add preflight check to ensure conntrack kernel module loaded; if not, try modprobe or annotate node and fail fast.
- Investigate containerd packaging change in infra-agent chart: why did binary differ across nodes? Is there a race where system updates apply post-launch?
- Update runbook for on-call: quick commands to restore (modprobe + restart kube-proxy, cordon/drain, helm rollback) and alert channels (Slack INF-channel, Jira INF ticket).

Notes to self (less formal):
- When draining, remember local-storage pod stuck => delete --force is ugly but necessary to unblock; log pod to find why it didn't delete.
- If kernel module missing across many nodes, probably AMI issue not helm. But mismatch + helm binary change is a dangerous combo.
- Keep captured SHA of golden containerd and add to infra repo as artifact to check during instance init.

Useful one-liners to paste into runbook:
- show node status + last events: kubectl get node -o wide && kubectl describe node <node> | egrep -A3 "Conditions:|Events:"
- quick kubelet log tail: sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
- force reload kube-proxy: kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy

End of scratchpad. Will convert to a short runbook once repro confirmed and packages validated.
